title: Garlic-Butter Filet
summary: Pan-seared filet with thyme butter, browned mushrooms, and crisp-edged roasted potatoes.

ingredients.item: olive oil, kosher salt, and black pepper

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 25–30 minutes, turning once, until browned and tender.
Pat the steaks dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat with a thin layer of oil. Sear the steaks for 2–3 minutes per side.
Add 2 tablespoons butter, half the garlic, and the herbs. Baste the steaks, then finish in the oven until they reach your preferred doneness. The package recommends 145°F followed by a 3-minute rest.
Rest the steaks. Cook the mushrooms in the same skillet until browned, then add the remaining butter and garlic.
Spoon the mushrooms over the steaks and serve with the roasted potatoes.
notes: The steak package serves two; the extra potatoes and mushrooms make the small leftover portion.
leftoverNote: Refrigerate the extra potatoes and mushrooms; reheat them in a skillet for lunch.

title: Cheddar-Herb Beef Pot Pie
summary: The prepared pot pie, finished with a bubbling sharp-cheddar and herb crust.

ingredients.item: frozen beef pot pie, thawed overnight

steps: Thaw the pot pie overnight in the refrigerator, then heat the oven to 400°F.
Remove the plastic wrap and place the tray on a sheet pan. Remove the crust temporarily and cover the filling with foil.
Heat the covered filling for 20 minutes.
Remove the foil, return the crust to the top, and bake for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle the crust with cheddar, herbs, and black pepper. Bake for another 5 minutes, or until the filling reaches 165°F.
Rest for 5–10 minutes before dividing into portions.
notes: These reheating steps follow the package directions, with cheddar and herbs added for the final five minutes.
leftoverNote: Reheat the remaining portion uncovered in a moderate oven to revive the crust.

title: Stroganoff Swedish Meatballs
summary: Prepared Swedish meatballs and spaetzle deepened with browned mushrooms, Dijon, and sour cream.

ingredients.item: parsley or dill and black pepper

steps: Heat the meatballs and spaetzle according to the package directions until hot throughout.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a skillet. Cook the mushrooms and onion for 8–10 minutes until deeply browned.
Lower the heat. Stir in the Dijon and several spoonfuls of gravy from the meatball tray.
Remove the skillet from the heat before stirring in the sour cream so it stays smooth.
Fold the mushroom sauce into the hot meatballs and spaetzle. Finish with herbs and black pepper.
notes: Do not boil the sauce after adding sour cream; high heat can make it split.
leftoverNote: Add a teaspoon of water before gently reheating the leftover portion.

title: Loaded Taco Bowls
summary: Seasoned ground beef over rice with black beans, corn, salsa, cheese, and avocado.

ingredients.item: salsa, shredded cheese, avocado, lime, and sour cream

steps: Cook the rice according to its package directions.
Brown the beef in a skillet, breaking it into small pieces. Drain excess fat if needed.
Add the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and 1/4 cup water. Simmer until the liquid has mostly evaporated and the beef reaches 160°F.
Warm the beans and corn.
Divide the rice, beef, beans, and corn among three bowls. Top with salsa, cheese, avocado, lime, and sour cream.
notes: Keep the avocado and other cold toppings separate from the leftover bowl until serving.
leftoverNote: Pack the third bowl for lunch, storing its cold toppings separately.

title: Caramelized-Onion Patty Melts
summary: Crisp rye, juicy smash patties, slow-cooked onions, Swiss cheese, and a swipe of Dijon.
steps: Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet over medium-low heat. Cook the onions with a pinch of salt for 20–25 minutes until deeply golden, then remove.
Season and cook the patties until browned and 160°F internally.
Build each melt with bread, Swiss cheese, a patty, onions, another slice of Swiss, and the second piece of bread. Butter the outsides.
Cook over medium-low heat until deeply toasted and the cheese has melted, about 3–4 minutes per side.
notes: Low heat gives the cheese time to melt before the bread gets too dark.
leftoverNote: Save the third cooked patty and onions separately; assemble and toast its sandwich fresh.

title: Flat-Iron Steak Fajitas
summary: Chile-lime steak sliced over charred peppers and onions with warm tortillas.
steps: Combine the spices, 1 tablespoon oil, lime juice, salt, and pepper. Rub the mixture over the steak.
Sear on a hot grill or skillet until it reaches your preferred doneness. The package recommends 145°F followed by a 3-minute rest.
Rest the steak for 10 minutes.
Cook the peppers and onion in the same skillet until browned but still slightly crisp.
Slice the steak thinly against the grain and serve with warm tortillas and toppings.
notes: The full 24-ounce steak makes four modest portions: dinner for two and lunch for two.
leftoverNote: Reheat the steak briefly so it does not overcook; the leftovers make excellent lunch tacos.

title: Mushroom-Swiss Burgers
summary: Thick grass-fed burgers with garlicky mushrooms, sweet onions, Swiss, and mustard mayo.
steps: Melt the butter in a skillet. Cook the mushrooms and onion for 8–10 minutes until browned, then season and remove.
Cook the patties on a grill or skillet until they reach 160°F.
Add Swiss cheese during the final minute and cover briefly to melt it.
Toast the buns and mix the mayonnaise with the Dijon.
Assemble each burger with mustard mayo, a patty, and the mushroom-onion mixture.
leftoverNote: Store the third patty, mushrooms, and bun separately so the bun stays dry.

title: Garlic-Parmesan Wings
summary: Oven-crisp wings tossed in roasted garlic butter, Parmesan, parsley, and lemon.
steps: Pat the thawed wings extremely dry. Heat the oven to 425°F and place a wire rack over a foil-lined sheet pan.
Toss the wings with baking powder, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Bake for 40–50 minutes, flipping halfway, until crisp and at least 165°F internally.
Melt the butter and briefly cook the fresh garlic without browning it.
Toss the hot wings with the garlic butter, Parmesan, lemon juice, and parsley.
notes: Use baking powder, not baking soda. Baking powder helps dry and crisp the skin.
leftoverNote: Reheat wings uncovered in a 400°F oven or air fryer so they stay crisp.

title: Baked Ziti Dinner
summary: Prepared baked ziti served as a complete Italian dinner with crisp garlic bread and Caesar salad.
steps: Heat the ziti according to its package directions until it reaches 165°F.
Mix the butter, garlic, and parsley. Spread over the cut bread.
Bake the bread at 400°F for 8–10 minutes. Broil briefly for additional browning if desired.
Chop the romaine and toss it with Caesar dressing, Parmesan, and croutons immediately before eating.
Serve the hot ziti with garlic bread and salad.
notes: Store the leftover salad components separately so the lettuce and croutons stay crisp.
leftoverNote: Refrigerate one portion of ziti; assemble its salad only when ready to eat.

title: Smoked Bacon Mac & Cheese
summary: The prepared tray exactly as intended: creamy, smoky, and reheated until bubbling.

ingredients.item: smoked bacon mac and cheese, thawed

steps: Thaw the tray in the refrigerator and heat the oven to 400°F.
Remove the lid or plastic wrap and place the tray on a sheet pan.
Cover with foil and heat for 20 minutes.
Remove the foil and cook for another 5–10 minutes, or until the center reaches 165°F.
Serve as-is.
notes: These are the heating directions printed on the package.
leftoverNote: Cover and refrigerate the remaining portion once cooled.

title: Homestyle Beef Stew
summary: The fully cooked beef stew, reheated and served without additions.
steps: Keep the stew frozen until ready to use, then thaw it in the refrigerator if directed by the sleeve.
Follow the package's microwave instructions; the exact time depends on its container and your microwave wattage.
Stir midway through reheating if the package directs you to do so.
Continue heating until the center reaches 165°F, then serve as-is.
notes: The front of the package identifies the stew as fully cooked and microwaveable. Follow the covered sleeve for its exact timing.
leftoverNote: Refrigerate the extra portion promptly and reheat it only once.

title: Bacon Breakfast Hash
summary: Crisp potatoes, smoky bacon, sweet peppers, and runny-yolk eggs from one skillet.

ingredients.item: Yukon Gold or red potatoes, diced

steps: Place the potatoes in a microwave-safe bowl with a splash of water. Cover and microwave for 4–5 minutes until partly tender, then drain and dry.
Cook the bacon in a large skillet until crisp. Remove it, leaving about 2 tablespoons fat.
Add the potatoes in an even layer. Cook for 10–12 minutes, turning only occasionally so they brown.
Add the onion, pepper, and paprika. Cook for another 6–8 minutes.
Return the bacon and season to taste. Fry two eggs for dinner and serve them over two portions of hash.
notes: Cook the third egg fresh when reheating the leftover hash.
leftoverNote: Reheat the remaining hash in a skillet and top it with a freshly cooked egg.

title: Lemon-Butter Scallops & Risotto
summary: Golden sea scallops with creamy Parmesan risotto, roasted asparagus, and bright lemon butter.

ingredients.item: olive oil, salt, and black pepper

steps: Pat the thawed scallops extremely dry and remove the small side muscles if present. Keep the broth warm in a saucepan.
Cook the shallot in 1 tablespoon butter. Add the rice and stir for 1–2 minutes.
Add the wine and let it absorb. Add warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring regularly and waiting for each addition to absorb. Continue for about 20 minutes.
Stir the Parmesan and 1 tablespoon butter into the risotto. Season and cover.
While the risotto cooks, toss the asparagus with oil, salt, and pepper. Roast at 425°F for 10–12 minutes.
Season the scallops. Heat a skillet over medium-high heat with a thin layer of oil. Sear without moving for 1 1/2–2 minutes per side, until golden, opaque, and firm.
Lower the heat. Add the remaining butter, garlic, lemon zest, and a squeeze of lemon. Spoon the butter over the scallops.
Divide the risotto, asparagus, and scallops among three plates.
notes: Dry scallops brown; wet scallops steam. Give them space and cook in two batches if necessary.
leftoverNote: The risotto reheats best with a splash of broth; warm the scallops very gently.
